clue.text: Letters to a girl in uniform giving directions?

definitions.text: Letters to a girl in uniform giving directions?

parts.words: Letters to a girl in uniform giving directions?
parts.note: mail sent to a Girl Guide (a uniformed member of the girls' scouting movement) reads as the name of a roadside pointer showing the way

explanation.surface: Someone writing to a uniformed girl, perhaps asking the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Letters' as POST and 'a girl in uniform' as a GUIDE, a member of the Girl Guides; together they name a signpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingerpost at a junction directs travellers, the job of the roadside sign named here.

clue.text: Rank of relative requiring an attendant

indicators.note: the relative needs another word to come along with it, here following it as an attendant

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member of some standing who needs a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a noun for status, but it is the adjective meaning foul; 'attendant' says the AN accompanies the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means foul or filthy, a synonym of impure.

clue.text: Get mad with some trader, angered beyond endurance

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words trader and angered are used, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: A merchant, furious past bearing, losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'traDER ANGEred'; 'beyond endurance' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone insane is to unhinge them, the sense of the verb here.

clue.text: Contumacious minister turned in by himself

indicators.note: the turned abbreviation goes inside the Latin phrase for by himself

parts.note: per se is Latin for by itself or by himself

indicators.note: the minister's abbreviation is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A stubborn clergyman who has turned in alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contumacious' is an old legal word for stubbornly defying authority; the clergyman of the surface has no part in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumacious means stubbornly disobedient, the same as wilfully contrary.

clue.text: A salad with excessively dull content

indicators.note: the word for dull is the content held within the word for excessively

parts.note: too means excessively
matt or mat means dull, without shine

explanation.surface: A salad whose contents are far too boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'satisfied' but means contents held inside; the salad is defined by its typical ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato is a typical salad vegetable, standing for the salad by example.

clue.text: Manufacturer of only the most basic wear

definitions.text: Manufacturer of only the most basic wear

parts.words: Manufacturer of only the most basic wear
parts.note: the most basic wear is read as what goes at the very base of the body, the feet, so this is a maker of footwear

explanation.surface: A clothing maker who produces only the simplest garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler makes footwear, which is worn at the body's base.

clue.text: European dogs' home?

parts.note: German shepherd dogs are named after a French border region, so their home would be that region, given in its old Latin form

explanation.surface: A kennel for dogs somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a kennel; the answer is the Latin name of Alsace, also once a slang name for a lawless sanctuary in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace, the French region the shepherd breed is named after, is in Europe; this is its Latin form.

clue.text: It's cheapest frequently on the North Sea coast

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing a place rather than naming it; the answer is a town there

parts.note: lowest means cheapest, of prices
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A remark that prices are often lowest by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: LOWESTOFT is a fishing town in Suffolk, on England's east coast facing the North Sea; 'It's' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: This Suffolk port and resort lies on the eastern English shore of the North Sea.

clue.text: A Moor has to return a greeting

indicators.note: the little word to is turned back on itself

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A North African who has to say hello back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses TO to make OT; Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Those keeping count may well get crosser

indicators.note: the word crosser may well be turned into another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: People tallying points tend to become angrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well get' signals that CROSSER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: People who keep the tally at a match record the points.

clue.text: Standard forms to state date of birth

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
your age is fixed by your date of birth

explanation.surface: Official forms ask you to give your birth date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forms' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard as an adjective means typical or normal, a synonym of ordinary.

clue.text: A merry celebration for vegetarians only?

definitions.text: A merry celebration for vegetarians only?

parts.words: A merry celebration for vegetarians only?
parts.note: a jolly party is read literally as a meal made only of pulses, fit for those who eat no meat

explanation.surface: A party where no meat is served.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEANFEAST is an old British word for a jolly celebration, originally an employer's annual dinner for workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolly party or spree, once an annual staff dinner, the literal reading suggesting pulses.

clue.text: Lads get upset about a girl being cut

indicators.note: the rearranged lads goes around the pronoun for a girl
the word lads is upset, its letters knocked into a new order

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: Boys become distressed about a girl who has been wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get upset' gives SLAD, and 'about' wraps it round the girl's pronoun; 'being' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slashed means gashed with a blade, a deep cut.

clue.text: Reliable person turning to a silly eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters of to a silly are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A dependable person going off to someone foolish and odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges TO A SILLY; 'turning' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone faithful and steadfast in their allegiance can be relied upon.

clue.text: Warning to a French minor

parts.note: un is French for a
less means smaller or minor

explanation.surface: A caution issued to a young French person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warning' is fair because 'unless' introduces a threatened condition: unless you stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction sets a condition and so serves as a caution of consequences.

clue.text: A round end is quite wrong, that's plain

indicators.note: quite wrong means utterly mistaken, so the letters of a round end are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A rounded ending is completely incorrect, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is quite wrong' rearranges A ROUND END; 'that's' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means without decoration, simple and bare.

clue.text: Quarrel a lot? Rubbish!

definitions.note: the exclamation stands for a dump where junk goes, used as a noun

parts.note: a scrap is a quarrel or fight
a heap is a lot, a large amount

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether people argue much and dismisses the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish!' looks like a scornful retort; it is the definition, the pile where discarded things go.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of discarded junk, the place for anything thrown out.

clue.text: A number leave no doubt of blame

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to ensure is to make certain, leaving no doubt

explanation.surface: Several people make certain whose fault it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blame' is the noun here: formal criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal reproof or condemnation, the noun sense of criticism.

clue.text: One may well upbraid salesman, a traveller

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
a rover is a wanderer or traveller

explanation.surface: A travelling sales rep who might tell someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition phrase stands for a person who scolds.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who scolds or rebukes someone does exactly that.

clue.text: Points to some duck grass

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south
part means some
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Directions given to a particular duck on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: ESPARTO is a coarse grass used in papermaking; 'to' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough Mediterranean grass used for rope and paper.

clue.text: Rambling royal letters go on and on

parts.note: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, are the Queen's royal initials
to rant is to go on and on loudly

explanation.surface: A monarch's correspondence goes on interminably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' means wandering, the old sense of errant as in knight errant.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering or roving, as a knight errant travels in search of adventure.

clue.text: Role almost totally absorbing new star of the stage

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: the shortened role takes in the rearranged word star
almost all of the word role is kept, its last letter lost
new means the letters of star are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Nearly a full part for a new acting star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives STRA. A rostrum is a speaker's platform, so 'of the stage' is a fair definition of the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a rostrum, the platform a speaker stands on.

clue.text: Born sound as a bell but in want

parts.note: née means born, used before a woman's maiden name
ding is the sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: A newborn in perfect health who still lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like 'in perfect health' but is the ringing noise; 'but' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking or requiring something, the state of being short.

clue.text: Tides can vary to a certain extent

indicators.note: vary means change, so the letters of tides can are changed in order

explanation.surface: Tides change only up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vary' rearranges TIDES CAN; 'to' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of space between two points, a measured extent.

clue.text: Youngsters in strict training caught arranging dates

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: arranging means putting in order, so the letters of dates are reordered

explanation.surface: Young people in rigorous training are caught fixing dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' rearranges DATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Young trainees in military or police instruction are under strict discipline.

clue.text: Director making a note on storage furniture

parts.note: D is a musical note
a dresser is a cupboard with shelves for crockery

explanation.surface: A film director produces a memo about a sideboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' is one who directs, as a letter is directed to an address; 'making' and 'on' join.
explanation.definitionFit: One who addresses a letter directs it to its recipient.

clue.text: Suffer when in the red stretched

indicators.note: the word for suffer goes inside the word red

parts.note: taken as written
to ache is to suffer pain

explanation.surface: Being overdrawn, someone feels strained and hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' looks like being overdrawn, but only 'red' supplies letters; 'when' and 'the' join.
explanation.definitionFit: Reached means extended an arm, as in stretched out for something.

clue.text: Go down and open one quietly

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
I is the Roman numeral one
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Sink, and then open something softly.
explanation.walkthrough: Overtip is used here to mean tip over, fall down.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple or keel over is to fall down.

clue.text: There is not now a brochure to bring out

parts.note: ex means former, something that no longer is
a tract is a pamphlet or brochure

explanation.surface: No pamphlet is left to hand out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There is not now' signals EX, meaning former; 'to' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw or pull something out, as a dentist removes a tooth.

clue.text: Outrage of bag, say, taken in to cause vexation

annotationWithheld.why: Outrage of bag, say, taken in to cause vexation: SAC (bag) + RILE (cause vexation) leaves GE, and 'say' gives EG with nothing to reverse it; no parse gives SACRILEGE from the clue as held (likely OCR loss)
annotationWithheld.clue: Outrage of bag, say, taken in to cause vexation
